title: Associated graded ring of an ideal
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $J\subseteq A$ an ideal, with $J^0=A$. The *associated graded ring* of $A$ with respect to $J$ is the abelian group $\operatorname{gr}_J(A)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}J^n/J^{n+1}$, whose elements are the finite sums $\sum_n\xi_n$ of homogeneous elements $\xi_n\in J^n/J^{n+1}$ of degree $n$, with the multiplication that is biadditive and given on homogeneous elements by $(a\bmod J^{n+1})\cdot(b\bmod J^{m+1})=ab\bmod J^{n+m+1}$ for $a\in J^n$, $b\in J^m$ (independent of the choices of $a,b$ since $J^{n+1}J^m+J^nJ^{m+1}\subseteq J^{n+m+1}$). It is a commutative ring with unit $1\bmod J$ in degree $0$, its degree-$0$ part $J^0/J^1=A/J$ is a subring, and it is an $A/J$-algebra through this subring. An ideal $\mathfrak b\subseteq\operatorname{gr}_J(A)$ is *homogeneous* if it contains the homogeneous components $\xi_n$ of each of its elements $\sum_n\xi_n$.
